{{Short description|English physicist (1922–1996)}}
'''William Keith Burton''' (known as Keith Burton<ref name=obit/>) [[FRSE]] (12 October 1922 – 30 December 1996) was an English electrical engineer and theoretical physicist.<ref name=obit>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rse.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/burton_william.pdf|title=William Keith Burton - Obituary |last=Wyllie|first=George|publisher=Royal Society of Edinburgh|archive-date=2015-06-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626115654/http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/obits_alpha/burton_william.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Alberty">{{cite book|last=Alberty|first=Robert A.|title=Thermodynamics of Biochemical Reactions|year=2003|publisher=John Wiley and Sons|isbn=978-0-471-22851-6|pages=2|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cxyBGj0rLAUC&pg=PA2}}</ref>

==Life==
He was born in [[Manchester]] and attended [[Manchester Grammar School]] prior to studying Electrical Engineering at Manchester College of Technology. After graduating he gained a job with [[General Electric Company plc|GEC]], first at [[Heywood, Greater Manchester|Heywood]], then [[Wembley]].<ref name=obit/>

From 1945 until 1951 he was employed as a theoretical physicist with [[Imperial Chemical Industries|ICI Ltd]], being seconded to [[Bristol University]] for the final 4 years, lecturing under [[Nevill Francis Mott]] and [[Herbert Fröhlich]]. From 1951 onwards he lectured in Natural Philosophy at [[Glasgow University]].

He developed the Burton–Carbrera–Frank model for [[adatom]]s and [[crystal growth]], with [[Nicolás Cabrera (physicist)|Nicolás Cabrera]] and [[Frederick Charles Frank]].<ref name="obit" />

He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] on 3 March 1958.<ref name=fellow>{{cite web | url = https://www.rse.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/all_fellows.pdf | title = Former RSE Fellows 1783 - 2002 | access-date = 2021-08-29 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210722142722/https://www.rse.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/all_fellows.pdf | archive-date = 2021-07-22 | url-status = live }}</ref>

He died at his home in [[Milngavie]] near [[Glasgow]] on 30 December 1996.
